title: Final host computation and head bound
statement: Let $M_V,M_I,M_P$ be finite Boolean Turing machines, let $x,u$ be Boolean words, let $c_t$ be an integer-indexed Boolean tape, and let $b$ be a Boolean value. Suppose $M_I$ computes the identity on $x$ in time $t_i$ and uses at most $s_i$ space at that time; suppose also that the cleaned simulation of $M_V$ on input $x$ followed by $u$ halts with output $b$, leaves its work tapes blank and heads at zero, and keeps every work-tape head within distance $s_v$ of zero throughout. Then, from the host configuration formed in its final-test phase using $x,u,c_t$ and zero initial offsets, the host machine halts with output $[b]$ after some finite number of steps, and every work-tape head stays within distance $|x|+|u|+s_v+s_i+1$ of zero throughout that run.
hypotheses_covered: $c_t$ is an integer-indexed optional Boolean tape
$M_I$ uses at most $s_i$ space on $x$ at time $t_i$
the cleaned simulation of $M_V$ on $x$ followed by $u$ has a clean run outputting $b$ with head bound $s_v$
caveat: The initial host configuration is specified through auxiliary constructions whose informal descriptions were not provided; the statement describes its phase and supplied data, but not the full tape layout.
